objectives.wording: Distinguish forensic medicine, clinical forensic medicine, forensic pathology, state medicine, legal medicine and medical jurisprudence using cases.
Trace major milestones linking medical evidence to legal practice.
Use the named Indian statutes to classify simulated civil and criminal cases, offence categories and police or magistrate inquests.
Locate an applicable official court or government publication and summarize its date, scope and implications for a simulated case.
Compare the jurisdiction and role of the courts, executive magistrates and Juvenile Justice Board named in the curriculum.

Describe court procedure for a medical witness, covering issue of summons, conduct money, types of witnesses, recording of evidence on oath or affirmation, examination-in-chief, cross-examination, re-examination, court questions and conduct in the witness box, and apply them in a role-play.
Explain perjury and the significance of judicial strictures for a medical witness.
Present a simulated expert opinion in court and distinguish findings, conclusions and limitations under questioning.
Compare dying declarations and dying depositions using simulated circumstances and documentation.
Demonstrate recording and certification in a simulated case and document the circumstances and capacity assessment.
Select and review records, registers and forms for sample cases involving discharge, injury, intoxication, fitness, death, cause-of-death certification and age estimation.
Select an underlying cause from a simulated causal sequence and verify its ICD-11 code.
Complete a simulated MCCD with the causal sequence, intervals and contributing conditions using the applicable form.
Review a simulated death and complete the medical cause-of-death certificate.
Distinguish somatic from cellular death and explain how the moment of death is determined.
Compare cortical and brainstem concepts of death and explain the legal criteria for certifying brainstem death.
Use the Indian transplantation framework to discuss consent, conflicts of interest and ethical safeguards in a simulated case.
Compare common mechanisms and explain which history and post-mortem evidence help distinguish them.
Classify representative deaths by manner and identify evidence that could change the assessment.
Distinguish timing and terminal physiological modes from the underlying cause of death.
Explain apparent death and identify circumstances that can mimic death in simulated cases.
Compare cooling, lividity, rigor, cadaveric spasm and cold or heat stiffening and explain their interpretive limits.
Compare decomposition, mummification, adipocere and maceration by circumstances and appearance.
Integrate several post-mortem observations with environmental context and report a range with uncertainty.
Compare clinical and medico-legal autopsies and explain how their objectives shape the examination.
Use a simulated case to identify authorization, documentation and examination requirements.
Explain how ancillary tests and imaging can help when gross examination does not establish a cause of death.
Plan documentation and preservation of clothing and viscera and distinguish representative artefacts from injuries.
Demonstrate respectful conduct, evidence handling and a clearly reasoned opinion in an autopsy simulation.
Assign roles and demonstrate coordination in simulated deaths involving alleged negligence, dowry-related circumstances, custody, human-rights concerns or exhumation.
Conduct supervised or simulated examinations and prepare reports for at least 15 varied causes.
Compare systemic and localised cold injuries by clinical features, post-mortem findings and medico-legal significance.
Compare heat-related injuries by clinical features, post-mortem findings and medico-legal significance.
Distinguish burns and scalds by mechanism, findings and medico-legal significance, including estimation of extent.
Distinguish electrocution, lightning and radiation injury by mechanism, findings and medico-legal significance.
Interpret representative clinical and post-mortem findings and explain what evidence is needed to assess neglect.
Use applicable NHRC guidance to plan documentation, examination and evidence handling in a simulated custodial death.
Describe authorization, recovery, documentation and specimen handling in a simulated exhumation.
Define the clinician's role at a simulated scene and use documented findings to propose a sequence of events and alternatives.
Plan a simulated investigation using clinical records, examination and collection and preservation of relevant evidence.
Adapt a simulated explanation of findings for peers, relatives, investigators and the court while respecting confidentiality.
Prepare a privacy-preserving response to a public or media enquiry.
Identify local resources and demonstrate how to coordinate them in a mass-fatality exercise.
Classify asphyxial mechanisms and interpret representative post-mortem findings in context, distinguishing supportive from nonspecific signs.
Compare the mechanism, clinical findings and post-mortem pattern of hanging and plan documentation.
Compare the mechanism, clinical findings and post-mortem pattern of ligature and manual strangulation and plan documentation.
Compare smothering, choking, gagging, traumatic and sexual asphyxia by mechanism and findings.
Compare representative drowning scenarios by pathophysiology and clinical and post-mortem findings, and assess the limits of individual findings.
Explain corpus delicti and distinguish measured or estimated identifying features from social descriptors that require independent documentation.
Compare hair, fibres, dental evidence and anthropometry for identifying unknown persons or remains, distinguishing trace associations from stronger identifiers.
Compare fingerprints, footprints, scars, tattoos, poroscopy and craniofacial superimposition by evidentiary role and limitations.
Outline inventory, examination and identification approaches for fragmented, charred and commingled remains.
Examine simulated remains and present a supported opinion with limitations.
Compare tooth eruption and decay as contextual findings in identification and explain the limitations of interpreting bite marks.
Integrate physical, dental and ossification findings in a simulated case and report an age range with uncertainty.
Prepare a simulated age-estimation report that states methods, findings and uncertainty.
Classify representative wounds and explain mechanisms and evidentiary limits when assessing defence or fabricated injuries.
Compare possible manners of injury, severity categories and findings that support antemortem or post-mortem timing.
Identify representative blunt, firearm, thermal and skeletal injuries and write supported medico-legal inferences.
Compare medical injury terminology with assault and hurt concepts using the applicable BNS text in a simulated case.
Compare wound and fracture healing and explain the limits of estimating injury age.
Draft a simulated wound report, identify factors affecting injury and healing, and distinguish direct and secondary causes of death.
Examine a simulated injured person and prepare a report documenting findings and reasoned opinion.
Compare representative weapon categories and explain how to document and preserve an item for examination.
Identify representative weapons and assess compatibility with supplied injury or post-mortem findings.
Identify major firearm and ammunition components and explain calibre, range and choke using diagrams.
Identify components of representative bullets and cartridges and explain what they support forensically.
Interpret representative firearm wound patterns and plan collection and preservation of evidence.
Interpret representative blast injury patterns and plan collection and preservation of evidence.
Localize and compare representative injuries of the head, neck, chest, abdomen, limbs, genitalia, spinal cord and skeleton.
Use simulated cases to distinguish impact sequences, crush syndrome and historical railway-spine terminology.
Locate the applicable BNS, BNSS and POCSO provisions and apply them to simulated scenarios involving care, examinations and reporting.
Analyze consent and representative nonconsensual acts in simulated cases and trace relevant changes in Indian law concerning sexuality and adultery.

In a simulated or supervised setting, examine an alleged accused in a sexual offence case, prepare the report, frame the opinion, preserve and dispatch trace evidence, and discuss how personal views can compromise objectivity and neutrality.
Plan a trauma-informed, consent-based examination and explain documentation, evidentiary limits and preservation and transfer of samples.
Demonstrate empathetic consent-based interviewing and examination in simulation, address support for minors and document findings and evidence custody.
Distinguish these concepts using a simulated case and explain which findings and records are needed.
Compare evidence of intrauterine death and live birth in a newborn.
Estimate gestational age from fetal findings and state the uncertainty.
Estimate fetal age from simulated post-mortem findings and report uncertainty.
Distinguish atypical interests from disorders using current DSM and ICD criteria and discuss consent and evidentiary limits in simulated cases.
Explain the medico-legal concept of legitimacy and draft a simulated court response explaining the scientific and ethical objections to virginity testing.
Compare evidence of pregnancy and of recent or remote delivery in living and deceased persons.
Explain how records and genetic testing can inform disputed maternity or paternity and identify limitations.
Identify the purposes of the PCPNDT Act and clinician responsibilities under it.
Identify the purposes of domestic violence law and clinician responsibilities under it.
Identify clinical documentation, referral and human-rights considerations in a simulated case.
Distinguish sexual dysfunction from infertility and compare representative causes and their medico-legal significance.
Explain the medico-legal significance of infertility.
Compare IVF and related reproductive interventions in representative medico-legal scenarios.
Explain the medico-legal aspects of artificial insemination.
Explain the medico-legal aspects of surrogacy.
Use the applicable Indian acts and rules to explain the regulation of surrogacy.
Use the applicable Indian acts and rules to compare registration, supervision and regulation of assisted reproduction.
Compare vasectomy and tubal procedures and describe their roles in the national family planning programme.
Classify abortion, compare methods and complications and use current official MTP provisions to analyze a simulated case.
Compare relevant findings in living and deceased persons and outline clinical duties and investigation of a suspected unlawful termination-related death.
Recognize concerning clinical and historical patterns and explain documentation and referral in a simulated safeguarding case.
Document representative injuries, discuss physical and psychological sequelae and outline survivor-centred care.
Locate applicable NHRC guidance and apply its documentation and examination requirements to a simulated case.
Conduct a simulated custody or court-referred examination using applicable NHRC guidance and prepare a report.
Demonstrate respectful communication and plan psychological support and rehabilitation in a simulated torture, human-rights violation or sexual assault case.
Explain support and referral needs in simulated assault, sexual violence, attempted suicide, homicide, domestic violence and dowry-related cases.
Trace the historical development of medical ethics and apply it to a clinical dilemma.
Explain the scope of bioethics using examples from care and research.
Apply autonomy, nonmaleficence, beneficence and justice to a simulated dilemma.
Explain the purpose of registration and verify a simulated practitioner record.
Compare the functions of the NMC and state councils.
Distinguish practitioner privileges, warnings, disciplinary proceedings and removal from the register.
Use the named ethics code and applicable updates to assess misconduct and fee splitting in simulated cases.
Map duties to patients and society to applicable legal and professional sources.
Demonstrate application of current professional rules in a simulated encounter.
Compare rights and duties and distinguish confidentiality from privileged communication.
Use the HIV and AIDS Act to analyse confidentiality, consent and discrimination in a simulated case.
Distinguish civil remedies, compensation and indemnity in a simulated healthcare claim using current sources.
Distinguish euthanasia, withholding or withdrawing treatment and DNR using applicable guidance and simulated cases.
Use current research guidance to identify consent, oversight and safety concerns in stem cell research.
Analyze barriers in a medico-legal encounter and propose communication and de-escalation strategies.
Identify sources of pressure in medico-legal work and select coping and escalation strategies.
Compare civil, criminal, contributory, corporate and vicarious concepts and analyze evidence, prevention and potential defences.
Compare types of consent and apply capacity, disclosure, voluntariness, age and emergency considerations.
Distinguish professional secrecy, therapeutic privilege and privileged communication.
Distinguish product liability from professional liability and explain the role of indemnity.
Compare Hippocratic, Charaka and Sushruta traditions and describe administration of an oath.
Relate commitments in the modified declaration to a clinical scenario.
Assess consent, risk, safeguards and oversight in a simulated clinical trial.
Compare applicable ethical safeguards and oversight for human and animal research.
Demonstrate how to design and document a simulated study using applicable ethics guidance.
Explain committee composition, review functions and ongoing oversight.
Classify representative mental disorders including PTSD using clinical features.
Distinguish delusions, hallucinations, illusions, lucid intervals and obsessions using examples.
Distinguish clinical diagnosis from civil capacity and criminal responsibility in simulated cases using applicable standards.
Compare corroborating evidence and limitations when evaluating possible feigned illness.
Explain its relationship to alcohol withdrawal and distinguish it from representative mimics.
Use the Mental Healthcare Act and applicable updates to examine admission, care and discharge in a simulated case.
Select appropriate living or post-mortem samples for representative analyses and explain Locard's exchange principle.
